evidence_quotes.agenda: 'What are your biggest concerns on this move? What are the most important...' — asked right after confirming his name, before logistics probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer stated 'the budget' as his biggest concern; the rep acknowledged it directly and promised to explain the value case, then wove that transparency through the whole pricing conversation, but never explicitly asked what his budget number was or what else he'd been quoted.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: None of the 5 lines reached — no rate-commit line, no estimate-variability restatement, no pay-less-if-faster line, no self-prep tip, no 'does that feel fair' check.

top_strength: Genuinely responsive to a budget-conscious, research-savvy customer (who cited Einstein's 4.9 rating back at the rep) — offered a free-reschedule morning slot to work around his not-yet-signed lease rather than pushing for an immediate afternoon booking.
coaching_note: When he named budget as his top concern, that was the cue to ask what he'd budgeted or what else he'd been quoted — instead the rep moved into the standard pitch, which is solid but generic against a customer who told you exactly what he's optimizing for. Total rounded from a raw component sum of 60.5 (half-point from a Stage 2 split).
